questions.stem: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on whether university canteens should be open to the public. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Recently, our university has been collecting opinions on whether campus canteens should welcome outside visitors. In my view, opening them to the public is a wise move that benefits both the campus and the community.

For one thing, university canteens usually offer clean and affordable meals, so opening them can relieve the dining pressure faced by nearby residents and office workers who struggle to find cheap lunches. For another, the extra income earned from these visitors allows canteens to upgrade their equipment and even lower prices for students. Admittedly, more diners may cause crowding and raise safety concerns; however, such problems can be eased by setting fixed visiting hours and checking visitors at the gate.

Therefore, I firmly believe that a properly managed open canteen is worthwhile. As long as student needs come first, sharing this resource makes our university a warmer part of society.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: Six people had to move away from their home to another place after a fire broke out in a building on Main Street Saturday, officials said. Firefighters responded to the three-story building shortly after 1 p.m. for a reported structure fire, according to Norwalk Deputy Fire Chief Adam Markowitz.
transcript.zh: 官员称,周六Main Street一栋建筑发生火灾后,六人不得不从家中搬到另一个地方。据Norwalk消防副局长Adam Markowitz称,消防员在下午1点刚过就接到建筑物火灾报告后赶到了这栋三层建筑。

transcript.text: Markowitz said crews encountered heavy smoke coming from the second floor when they arrived. A team of about 25 firefighters then spent about 25 minutes extinguishing the flames. Officials described the structure as a mixed-use building that features commercial businesses on the first floor and residential on the second and third floors.
transcript.zh: Markowitz说,消防人员到达时遇到从二楼冒出的浓烟。随后约25名消防员组成的队伍花了大约25分钟扑灭了火焰。官员将该建筑描述为一栋混合用途建筑,一楼为商业店铺,二楼和三楼为住宅。

transcript.text: Town records list four apartments in the building. Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were declared uninhabitable, and the six residents had to move to another place, officials said. No injuries were reported in connection with the fire. The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.
transcript.zh: 城镇记录显示该建筑内有四套公寓。官员称,由于烟雾和高温破坏,这四套公寓被宣布不适宜居住,六名居民不得不搬到另一个地方。没有关于火灾造成人员伤亡的报告。Norwalk消防局长正在调查火灾的原因和起源。

questions.stem: Why did the six residents have to find another place to stay?

options.text: Due to a fire alarm in their apartments.
Because of the smoke and heat damage.
Due to the water used to extinguish the flames.
Because of the collapse of the three-story building.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were declared uninhabitable, and the six residents had to move to another place, officials said.信号：因果信号 Due to 引出原因 。答案句以 Due to smoke and heat damage 开头，Due to 是明确的因果信号，紧接着就是结果 the six residents had to move…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说因 a fire alarm in their apartments（公寓里的火警铃）。录音确实通篇讲 fire（火灾），但从没说居民因为「火警铃响」才搬走，搬离的真正原因是烟热损坏。它借你对 fire 的耳熟来骗选。 借用原文：extinguishing the flames
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 说因 the water used to extinguish the flames（灭火用的水）。录音里确有 extinguishing the flames（扑灭火焰）这个动作，但只讲了灭火过程，从没说「水渍」让公寓不能住。它盗用 extinguish the flames 制造熟悉感。 借用原文：the three-story building
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说因 the collapse of the three-story building（三层楼坍塌）。录音确有 the three-story building（三层楼）这个词，但全文只字未提坍塌，反而说 No injuries were reported（无人受伤）。它盗用 three-story building，再编一个没发生的「坍塌」。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Due to smoke and heat damage ↔ Because of the smoke and heat damage Due to 与 Because of 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were declared uninhabitable, and the six residents had to move to another place, officials said.

questions.stem: What does the news report say the Norwalk Fire Marshal is doing?

options.text: Investigating the cause of the incident.
Helping search for the suspect of the crime.
Rescuing the businessmen trapped in the building.
Checking town records for the property developer.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.信号：主体名 Fire Marshal 后的动作 。录音末句直接出现题目要找的主体 The Norwalk Fire Marshal，紧跟其后的动词 is investigating the cause and origi…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 说在 Helping search for the suspect of the crime（帮忙搜捕嫌犯）。录音通篇是火灾事故，没有任何「嫌犯 / 犯罪」字眼，消防局长做的是调查起因，不是抓人。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 说在 Rescuing the businessmen trapped in the building（营救被困商人）。录音确实提到一楼有 commercial businesses（商铺），但明说 No injuries were reported（无人受伤），根本没人被困需救。它借 businesses 谐想出 businessmen 来诱选。 借用原文：Town records list four apartments in the building
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 说在 Checking town records for the property developer（为开发商查市镇记录）。录音确有 Town records list four apartments（市镇记录列有四套公寓）这一句，但 town records 只是新闻引用的信息来源，消防局长做的是调查起因，没人「为开发商查记录」。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（investigating the cause and origin of the fire ↔ Investigating the cause of the incident the fire 概括为 the incident）

questions.evidenceText: The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.

transcript.text: A new study has cast doubt on historic research suggesting that the season or month of someone's birth is associated with an increased risk of certain mental health conditions. The study looks at symptoms of anxiety and depression among more than 70,000 older adults in Europe.
transcript.zh: 一项新研究对历史研究提出了质疑,这些历史研究认为某人的出生季节或月份与某些心理健康状况的风险增加有关。该研究调查了欧洲超过7万名老年人的焦虑和抑郁症状。

transcript.text: A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses. Researchers have suggested that such links could arise from various things. These include nutrient intake, sun exposure, climate, and disease exposure varying across the course of the year. However, evidence has been mixed. More recent studies have suggested that factors such as social class or economic background have more to do with these diagnoses than month of birth.
transcript.zh: 过去的许多研究发现了出生季节与心理健康诊断之间的联系。研究人员认为,这种联系可能源于各种因素。这些因素包括全年不同时期的营养摄入、阳光照射、气候和疾病暴露的变化。然而,证据一直是混杂的。最近的研究表明,社会阶层或经济背景等因素与这些诊断的关系比出生月份更大。

transcript.text: Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety. There was some variability in some countries. In Poland, depressive symptoms fluctuated a little depending on birth month. In the Czech Republic, the same was true of anxiety symptoms. But on the whole, there was no systematic pattern.
transcript.zh: 总体而言,这项新研究发现参与者的出生月份与抑郁或焦虑症状之间没有显著关系。在一些国家存在一些变化。在波兰,抑郁症状根据出生月份有轻微波动。在捷克共和国,焦虑症状也是如此。但总的来说,没有系统性模式。

questions.stem: What have a number of past studies found about season of birth?

options.text: It plays a less important role in one's health than nutrient intake.
It impacts people's health to a lesser degree than sun exposure.
It is associated with people's mental health conditions.
It is linked with older adults' symptoms of depression.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses.信号：主语原样复现作信号 。题干主语 a number of past studies 在录音第 2 段以 A number of past studies have found 几乎原样出现，这一「问谁就听谁」的主体复现…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 用了录音第 2 段确实念到的 nutrient intake 一词，但录音只是把它列为「关联可能的成因之一」，从没说出生季节「在健康中作用不及营养摄入」。A 把它编成一句子虚乌有的轻重比较，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：These include nutrient intake, sun exposure, climate, and disease exposure
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 借用录音里同样念到的 sun exposure，谎称出生季节「对健康的影响不及日晒」。录音把 sun exposure 与 nutrient intake 并列为可能成因，并未拿它和出生季节比影响大小，属偷换概念式的原词陷阱。 借用原文：symptoms of anxiety and depression among more than 70,000 older adults
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 说关联的是 older adults' symptoms of depression。录音中「老年人」与「抑郁/焦虑症状」出现在介绍新研究样本（more than 70,000 older adults）与总结处，并非「过往研究就出生季节发现的关联对象」；过往研究发现的是更宽的 mental health diagnoses。D 把答案的范围从「心理健康」窄化到「老年人的抑郁症状」，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses ↔ associated with people's mental health conditions link=associated、diagnoses≈conditions）

questions.evidenceText: A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses.

questions.stem: What did the new study find about the relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety.信号：总结词 Overall + 否定 no significant 。段首的 Overall 是结论信号，提示这句是新研究的总判断；其后的 no significant relationship 用「否定 + 程度词」给…

optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：A 说 It was indefinite.（不确定的）。录音其实给出了明确结论——「没有显著关联」「没有系统性规律」，态度是确定的「无」，并非含糊不定。把「确定地没有」错听成「不确定」，是对结论性质的误判。
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：B 用了录音末句确实念到的 systematic，可原文是 no systematic pattern（没有系统性规律），带否定。B 抹掉 no，单取 systematic 说成「它是系统性的」，正好与原文意思相反，是典型听到原词就选、却漏听否定词的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 说 It was straightforward.（直接明了的）。录音从未用「直接/明了」评价这关系，只说「无显著关联、无系统规律，部分国家有些小波动」。这个定性原文根本没出现，属凭空臆造。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（no significant relationship ↔ It was insignificant. no significant=insignificant）

questions.evidenceText: Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants' month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety.

transcript.text: Genetic researchers in China have made a clone of a star police dog. The clone was born in a laboratory in Beijing in December. Tests show that the clone and her mother are almost identical genetically. The mother dog helped solve multiple murders and many other crimes. The clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests.
transcript.zh: 中国的遗传研究人员克隆了一只明星警犬。该克隆犬于12月在北京的一个实验室出生。测试显示,克隆犬与其母犬在基因上几乎完全相同。母犬曾协助侦破多起谋杀案和许多其他犯罪案件。克隆犬已经在多项测试中表现得优于传统繁育的犬只。

transcript.text: If the clone continues to perform as well as expected, it could mean a huge reduction in the training time for police dogs, which usually takes about five years. The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones of talented police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years. However, this goal is not yet possible due to the current costs of the technology.
transcript.zh: 如果克隆犬继续按预期表现良好,这可能意味着警犬训练时间的大幅缩减,而警犬训练通常需要约五年时间。科学家的最终目标是培育出优秀警犬的克隆体,使其能够在数月而非数年内完成训练。然而,由于目前该技术的成本,这一目标尚无法实现。

transcript.text: This is not the first time a clone has been made of a star police dog. In South Korea, six clones began working with the police in 2008.
transcript.zh: 这并非首次克隆明星警犬。在韩国,六只克隆犬于2008年开始与警方合作。

questions.stem: What do the researchers' tests show about the cloned dog?

options.text: It has helped solve several murder cases.
It has become a star office dog in Beijing.
It has surpassed its mother in performance.
It has done better than naturally born dogs.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests.信号：tests一词复现即落点 。题干问的是 tests 显示什么，录音第一段末句 performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests 正好出现 t…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：It has helped solve several murder cases. 偷用了录音里 helped solve multiple murders 的'破案'信息，但原文说破案的是 The mother dog（母亲），不是这只克隆犬，把母亲的功劳安到了克隆犬头上。 借用原文：The clone was born in a laboratory in Beijing in December.
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：It has become a star office dog in Beijing. 拼接了录音里的 star（明星）和 Beijing（北京）两个原词，但原文只说克隆犬生于北京实验室、母亲是明星警犬，从没说克隆犬变成了'办公室明星狗'，属拼凑+无中生有。 借用原文：the clone and her mother are almost identical genetically
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：It has surpassed its mother in performance. 利用了原文反复提到的 mother（母亲），但录音说克隆犬与母亲 almost identical genetically（基因几乎相同），并没说它在表现上'超过'了母亲；它超过的是普通狗，不是母亲。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（traditionally bred dogs ↔ naturally born dogs 传统繁育=自然出生）

questions.evidenceText: The clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests.

questions.stem: What is the scientists' purpose in cloning police dogs?

options.text: To speed up investigation into criminal cases.
To test the feasibility of cloning technology.

questions.analysis: 目的题。答案句（P2）：The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones of talented police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years.信号：ultimate goal点出目的句 。录音第二段 The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones 用 goal（目标）直接亮明目的，这正是目的题要等的那句话…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：To speed up investigation into criminal cases. 借了第一段 crimes（犯罪）的余味，但录音讲的目的是缩短训练时间，从没说克隆是为了'加快案件调查'，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：To test the feasibility of cloning technology. 听起来很像科研口吻，但录音里克隆的目的是缩短训练时间，并没说'是为了测试克隆技术是否可行'，是凭常识想当然添上的目的。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：To cut down training expenses. 与正解只差一个词：录音说的是省'时间'（months instead of years），不是省'费用'。原文里 costs（成本）出现在最后一句、说的是'技术成本高导致目标暂不可行'，是障碍、不是目的，被挪来当目的了。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（trained in months instead of years ↔ reduce their training time 几月而非几年=缩短时间）

questions.evidenceText: The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones of talented police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years.

questions.stem: Why does the news report say the scientists' goal is not yet possible?

options.text: Cloning is too complicated a process.
The technology is yet to be accepted.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：However, this goal is not yet possible due to the current costs of the technology.信号：However转折加due to因果 。录音第二段末句先用 However 转折（前面说目标美好、这里说还做不到），再用 due to the current costs of the technology 给出原因…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Cloning is too complicated a process. 听上去像个合理障碍，但录音明确把原因归到'成本'（costs），从没说过程'太复杂'，是凭常识猜的障碍。
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：The technology is yet to be accepted. 借用了录音 not yet possible（还不可行）里 yet 的语感，但原文说做不到是因为贵，不是因为'还没被接受'，属偷换原因。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：Cloning is ethically controversial. 是一般人一提'克隆'就联想到的伦理争议，但本则新闻只说障碍是成本，完全没提伦理，是被话题带偏的想当然选项。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the current costs of the technology ↔ The technology is too expensive. 成本高=太贵）

questions.evidenceText: However, this goal is not yet possible due to the current costs of the technology.

transcript.text: W: Tom, did you see the article online about the new TV series based on the book The Three Body Problem?
transcript.zh: W: Tom，你看到网上关于根据《三体》这本书改编的新电视剧的文章了吗？

transcript.text: M: A colleague mentioned the book, but I've been so busy writing my thesis that I haven't been able to read for pleasure in months.
transcript.zh: M: 有同事提到过这本书，但我一直忙着写论文，已经好几个月没能读闲书了。

transcript.text: W: Well, sounds like if you're going to read anything for fun, this is the book. It's written by a Chinese science fiction writer. I can't remember his name, but he's written three books in all, and The Three Body Problem is the first in the series. I don't want to say too much and spoil it for you, but it's definitely got some amazing technological and sociological concepts in it.
transcript.zh: W: 听起来如果你要读点消遣的东西，就该读这本书。它是一位中国科幻作家写的。我记不得他的名字了，但他一共写了三本书，《三体》是系列的第一部。我不想说太多剧透，但里面确实有一些很棒的技术和社会学概念。

transcript.text: M: It does sound like it would suit my taste, but if they are making a TV series based on it now, I don't know if I should read the book or watch the show first.
transcript.zh: M: 听起来确实符合我的口味，但如果他们现在要根据它拍电视剧，我不知道该先读书还是先看剧。

transcript.text: W: I think it's better to read the book first. It's rare for the show or movie to be better than the book. And then, you just end up ruining the book for yourself, if the show isn't very good.
transcript.zh: W: 我觉得最好先读书。电视剧或电影比书好的情况很少见。而且如果剧拍得不好，你就把书给毁了。

transcript.text: M: When is the show supposed to start? I'm a bit overwhelmed with the amount of data I still need to collect to finish my thesis. But I still need to relax sometimes.
transcript.zh: M: 这个剧什么时候开播？我现在还有大量数据要收集才能完成论文，有点应接不暇。但我还是需要偶尔放松一下。

transcript.text: W: I can't remember exactly. It's pretty soon, and it's going to be quite long. There are 24 episodes. Well, maybe you could download an electronic copy of the book and try to read it before the show starts.
transcript.zh: W: 我记不太清了。挺快的，而且会很长。有24集。也许你可以下载电子版的书，在剧开播前试着读完。

transcript.text: M: That's a good idea. And then, maybe we can watch the series together. Thanks for the tip, Alice.
transcript.zh: M: 这主意不错。然后也许我们可以一起看这部剧。谢谢你的建议，Alice。

transcript.text: W: No problem.
transcript.zh: W: 不客气。

questions.stem: How did the man get to know about the book The Three Body Problem?

options.text: He heard about it from a coworker.
He read an article reviewing it.
He watched a TV series based on it.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：A colleague mentioned the book, but I've been so busy writing my thesis that I haven't been able to read for pleasure in months.信号：被问者的直接应答 。上一句女士问起这书，男士开口第一句就是 A colleague mentioned the book——对话题里答案就落在被问者的应答上，这句正面回答了「怎么知道的」，是答案句。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：女士开场说 did you see the article online，选项 He read it somewhere online. 把这个 online 搬过来，但「网上看到」的主语是女士的提问、说的是那篇文章，不是男士得知书的途径，属答非所问。 借用原文：the article online about the new TV series
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：录音里的 the article online about the new TV series 是讲改编剧的报道，选项 He read an article reviewing it. 偷换成「读了一篇评论这本书的文章」，且读文章的是女士不是男士，既偷换内容又张冠李戴。 借用原文：the new TV series based on the book
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：录音通篇说剧还没看、甚至还没开播（When is the show supposed to start?），选项 He watched a TV series based on it. 说他「看了改编剧」与事实相反，男士并没看过剧。

transcript.text: Supporters call it "wild camping"; opponents call it "illegal camping". What both sides accept is that there has been a boom in the past few months, with increasing numbers of visitors pitching their tents on any bit of land they fancy in the UK. In part, this reflects the fact that official campsites have been wholly or partially closed, or are overflowing in a summer when fewer people are going abroad. It is also cheap, at a time when many are worried about what the economic future holds. But it may also be an expression of a desire for going outdoors—a response to the months of lockdown.
transcript.zh: 支持者称之为"野外露营"；反对者称之为"非法露营"。双方都承认的是，过去几个月出现了激增现象，越来越多的游客在英国任何他们看中的土地上搭起帐篷。这在一定程度上反映了一个事实，即官方露营地已经全部或部分关闭，或者在这个出国人数较少的夏天已经人满为患。在许多人担心未来经济前景的时候，这也很便宜。但这也可能是一种对户外活动渴望的表达——一种对数月封锁的回应。

transcript.text: Most of the coverage of the boom in wild camping has been negative. Camping in public parks has now been banned for August and the early part of September because campers dump litter, human waste, and even their tents on the grassland. Similar action has been taken even in Scotland, where camping is usually permitted on most of its open land.
transcript.zh: 关于野外露营热潮的大部分报道都是负面的。由于露营者在草地上倾倒垃圾、人类排泄物甚至他们的帐篷，公共公园现已禁止在8月和9月初进行露营。即使在苏格兰也采取了类似的行动，而那里通常允许在其大部分开放土地上露营。

transcript.text: Clearly there have to be rules. It would make sense that wild campers need to ask for permission to camp from landowners, especially outside Scotland, where the law is far more restrictive. It would be common sense for people to use small tents and leave no trace of their visit. They have been attracted by a patch of land this close to wilderness, and it is their responsibility to keep it that way.
transcript.zh: 显然必须有规则。野外露营者需要向土地所有者征求露营许可是合理的,特别是在苏格兰以外的地区，那里的法律要严格得多。人们使用小帐篷并不留下任何访问痕迹是常识。他们被这片如此接近荒野的土地所吸引，保持其原貌是他们的责任。

transcript.text: Imagine boating down the Amazon River, minding your own business—calmly keeping an eye out for alarmingly large snakes—and a curious pink dolphin appears to swim alongside. While this may seem like a mythical creature, pink dolphins do exist in the Amazon region.
transcript.zh: 想象一下，你正在亚马逊河上划船，专心做着自己的事——平静地留意着那些大得惊人的蛇——这时一只好奇的粉红色海豚出现在你身边游动。虽然这看起来像是神话中的生物，但粉红色海豚确实存在于亚马逊地区。

transcript.text: The Amazon river dolphin is a giant among its species. It can measure up to 2 meters long and weigh around 204 kilograms. Size isn't the only thing that sets the Amazon river dolphin apart. Thriving in South American rivers and temporary lakes caused by seasonal flooding, this freshwater dolphin is sometimes shockingly pink.
transcript.zh: 亚马逊河豚是其物种中的巨型成员。它的体长可达2米，体重约204千克。体型并不是亚马逊河豚与众不同的唯一特征。这种淡水豚栖息在南美洲的河流和季节性洪水形成的临时湖泊中，有时会呈现出令人震惊的粉红色。

transcript.text: Although born gray, males of the species are easily identified as they enter adulthood by a decisive pink shade. Their unusual coloring is believed to be the result of scar tissue from dolphin fights—whether playful fighting or a serious bid for a mate. The deeper the pink, the more attractive the males are believed to be, and the older the male, the more pink it will have.
transcript.zh: 虽然出生时是灰色的，但该物种的雄性在进入成年期后很容易通过明显的粉红色阴影来识别。它们不寻常的颜色被认为是海豚打斗留下的疤痕组织的结果——无论是嬉戏打闹还是为争夺配偶的激烈竞争。粉红色越深，雄性被认为越有吸引力，而雄性年龄越大，粉红色就越多。

transcript.text: There's also a theory that this color helps the dolphins more readily blend in with their surroundings. During heavy rains, rivers along the Amazon rainforest turn a pink shade, and with it male dolphins are harder to detect. transcript.zh: 还有一种理论认为，这种颜色有助于海豚更容易地与周围环境融为一体。在大雨期间，亚马逊雨林沿岸的河流会呈现粉红色，雄性海豚也因此更难被发现。由亚马逊河滋养的亚马逊湿地系统是粉红色海豚繁殖的关键场所，自2018年以来已被授予国际保护地位。

transcript.text: In a new Merrill Lynch/Age Wave survey, a full 70% of the early adults said they received financial support from their parents in the past year and 58% said they couldn't afford their current lifestyles without it. The most common types of financial support include cell phone plans, food, school costs and car expenses. Parental financial support of early adults, said Ken Dychtwald, CEO of Age Wave, is "the new normal".
transcript.zh: 在 Merrill Lynch/Age Wave 的一项新调查中，70% 的年轻成年人表示他们在过去一年中得到了父母的经济支持，58% 的人表示如果没有这些支持，他们无法负担目前的生活方式。最常见的经济支持类型包括手机套餐、食物、学费和汽车开支。Age Wave 首席执行官 Ken Dychtwald 表示，父母对年轻成年人的经济支持是"新常态"。

transcript.text: But 64% of the young adults surveyed said parents' financial support to children age 25 to 34 is "a bad thing", because it makes those kids dependent. By contrast, only 29% thought supporting men and women age 18 to 24 is bad; the remaining 71% think that assistance "helps the adult children get ahead".
transcript.zh: 但 64% 接受调查的年轻成年人表示,父母对 25 至 34 岁子女的经济支持是"坏事",因为这会让这些孩子产生依赖性。相比之下,只有 29% 的人认为支持 18 至 24 岁的男性和女性是坏事;其余 71% 的人认为这种援助"帮助成年子女取得进步"。

transcript.text: Dychtwald believes the young women and men surveyed were saying that by 25, younger adults ought to be financially independent. In fact, the respondents said, financial independence defines adulthood. "Financial independence is something they were struggling with and challenged by. And it scared them a bit," Dychtwald said. One big reason they're struggling is attributed to college loans, of which the average amounts to $37,000. Many of the parents have taken on college loans for the kids, too, sometimes at the expense of their own finances. In the survey, 60% of early adults define financial success as being debt-free. Whether that's likely, or even possible, anytime soon is anyone's guess.
transcript.zh: Dychtwald 认为,接受调查的年轻女性和男性表达的意思是,到 25 岁时,年轻成年人应该在经济上独立。事实上,受访者表示,经济独立定义了成年。"经济独立是他们正在努力应对和面临挑战的事情。这让他们有点害怕," Dychtwald 说。他们面临困难的一个重要原因归结于大学贷款,平均金额为 37,000 美元。许多父母也为孩子承担了大学贷款,有时以牺牲自己的财务状况为代价。在调查中,60% 的年轻成年人将经济成功定义为无债务。这是否可能,甚至是否有可能在短期内实现,谁也说不准。

Over the coming decades, millions of jobs will be threatened by robotics and artificial intelligence. Despite intensive academic 26______ on these developments, there has been little study on how workers 27______ to being replaced through technology.

To find out, business researchers at TUM and Erasmus University Rotterdam conducted 11 studies and surveys with over 2,000 persons from several countries.

The findings show: In principle, most people view it more 28______ when workers are replaced by other people than by robots or intelligent software. This preference 29______ , however, when it refers to people's own jobs. When that is the case, the majority of workers find it less upsetting to see their own jobs go to robots than to other employees. In the long term, however, the same people see machines as more threatening to their future role in the workforce. These effects can also be observed among people who have recently become unemployed.

The researchers were able to identify the causes behind these 30______ paradoxical results, too: People tend to 31______ themselves less with machines than with other people. Consequently, being replaced by a robot or software 32______ less of a threat to their feeling of self-worth. This reduced self-threat could even be observed when participants assumed that they were being replaced by other employees who relied on technological abilities such as artificial intelligence in their work.

"Even when unemployment results from the 33______ of new technologies, people still judge it in a social context," says Christoph Fuchs, one of the authors of the study. "It is important to understand these 34______ effects when trying to manage the massive changes in the working world to minimize 35______ in society."

应填 D) debate
【原文】学术辩论与「研究 little study」对照
J) modifications 「修改」与 academic 搭配不通：academic modifications「学术修改」不是常规表达，也无法与下半句 little study 形成让步逻辑。

questions.analysis:
【答案】M（官方答案）
应填 M) react
【原文】react to 固定搭配「对……做出反应」
A) compare compare 常用搭配是 with，不是 to being replaced：compare 后接 to 多用于比喻类比（compare A to B），不能讲「工人比较被替代」；语义上「研究工人怎样比较被替代」也讲不通。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 28.
questions.analysis:
【答案】G（官方答案）
应填 G) favorably
【原文】view ... favorably 是固定搭配「赞许地看待」

O) seemingly 「看似」无法被 more 修饰：seemingly 表「表面上」，不带比较级语义，more seemingly 也不构成自然表达，且该词另有更贴合的空位归宿。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 29.
questions.analysis:
【答案】N（官方答案）
应填 N) reverses
【原文】前一句说「人们普遍更接受被人取代」，本句却用 however 引出「轮到自己时，大家反而觉得被机器取代不那么糟」，preference 完全反转，正是 reverses「逆转」的语义。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 30.

【答案】O（官方答案）

F) drastically 「极度地」修饰 paradoxical 程度过强：drastically paradoxical「极度矛盾」语义太满，与下文用心理机制平稳解释的论述基调不合；研究者既然能解释，矛盾就不是极端的。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 31.

【答案】A（官方答案）
应填 A) compare

compare oneself with/to「把自己与……比较」是高频搭配；句意「人们倾向于把自己与机器比较得少」恰好解释下一句 poses less of a threat「威胁感更弱」的因果。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 32.
questions.analysis:
【答案】K（官方答案）
应填 K) poses
【原文】pose a threat 固定搭配「构成威胁」
B) contradicts 「反驳」与 threat 不搭配：contradict a threat 不构成搭配，且语义上「被替代反驳威胁」讲不通。
N) reverses 「逆转」语义错位且要留给 29 题：reverse a threat「逆转威胁」语义牵强；且 29 题 This preference ___ 明显需要 reverses「逆转」的呼应，应预留。

【答案】I（官方答案）
应填 I) introduction
【原文】the introduction of new technologies「新技术的引入/推出」是 unemployment results from 的合理原因——技术引入才会替代人力，逻辑链通顺。
E) disruptions 搭配冲突且要留给 35 题：disruptions of new technologies 不是惯常表达（更常说 disruptions caused by technologies）；且 35 题 mini

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Certain institutions, such as schools, are likely to close when bad weather, such as snow, flooding or extreme heat or cold, causes travel difficulties, power outages(断供), or otherwise endangers public safety. When snowy weather arrives in the US, it means the chance of school children benefiting from the long-standing tradition of the "snow day", when schools are forced to close and students get an unexpected day off.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The criterion for a snow day is primarily the inability of school buses to operate safely on their routes and danger to children who walk to school. Often, the school remains officially open even though buses do not run and classes are canceled. Severe weather that causes cancellation or delay is more likely in regions that are less able to handle the situation. Snow days are less common in more northern areas of the United States that are used to heavy winter snowfall, because municipalities are well equipped to clear roads and remove snow. In areas less accustomed to snow even small snowfalls of an inch or two may render roads unsafe.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Snow days are a familiar theme in American film and TV shows, with children getting the good news and then running outside for some seasonal snowman-building and snowball throwing, against a background of joyful pop music. But the tradition is now over for pupils in several US states such as South Carolina, Nevada, Georgia and Indiana. This academic year, many school boards have introduced policies which require students to work from home if the school is shut by snow or extreme weather. They are known as "e-learning days", which certainly sounds less fun than a snow day.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Teachers are also losing their snow days and instead will be expected to be on hand to take a virtual register and answer students' questions online. A pilot programme in a school district in Anderson County, South Carolina, has supplied students with electronic tablets loaded with assignments to complete in the event of a school closure. If it is successful, it could be rolled out across the state.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: But some parents object to the new policy if the vigorous debate on the Facebook page of Anderson County school district is anything to go by. "When it snows, let the kids enjoy it," said one commenter. Another said the decision would "ruin school even more", and someone else called snow days "a fun part of childhood". But supporters of the policy say it means children will miss fewer days of school. It will also bring to an end a less popular US high school tradition: the "make-up day", which requires students in many states to make up the time lost due to weather by working during school holidays.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Students in North Carolina already have several make-up days scheduled because of school closures during Hurricane Florence, which struck in September. Tom Wilson, the superintendent(主管) of Anderson County school district, said the change away from snow days makes practical and financial sense. He said technology has changed every profession, so it makes sense to use it to "eliminate" make-up days. Adam Baker of the Department of Education in Indiana said e-learning days were proving a "great success". He said most Indiana schools already use digital devices during lessons, so it was an "easy decision" to extend this to days when schools are closed. He denies the decision is depriving children of the chance to enjoy the snow. "Students are still able to enjoy snow days and outside time," he said. "Many have PE and science assignments that have them out enjoying the weather." But local school superintendents in Ohio are resisting proposals to adopt e-learning days. They fear that students without internet access at home will be disadvantaged by the policy, and superintendent Tom Roth is concerned that e-learning days will offer a lower quality of education.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: There are also so-called "blizzard bags", with assignments that children take home ahead of an expected snow closure. But Mr Roth says it is not sufficient as a replacement. "I think we still need the class time to give our kids the education that they deserve," he said. "You can't get that with a blizzard bag or doing the work from home like that. It's not going to be as effective."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: There is a long-running debate on whether missing days of school affects attainment. In England, there has been a focus on tackling absenteeism(旷课) from school. The Department for Education (DFE) published research in 2016 arguing that missing any days at school could have a negative impact on results. Even a few days lost in a year could be enough to miss out on getting a good exam grade, the DFE's research concluded. This differed from the findings of a study from Harvard University in the US, which concluded that missing a few occasional days because of the weather did not damage learning.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The Harvard study examined seven years of school results data and could not find any impact from snow closures. What caused more disruption was when schools tried to stay open in bad weather, even though many staff and pupils were absent. But weather can make a difference to school results, according to another piece of Harvard research published last summer. It's hot weather that has the negative impact. The results of 10 million school students were examined over 13 years and researchers found a "significant" link between years with extremely hot weather and lower results.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: It's obvious that students should go to school every day to get the most out of education. In cases of extreme weather students don't always have that option. However, research shows that authorised absences from school such as during extreme weather are less problematic for students than absences that are not authorised. This is because unauthorised absences tend to reflect patterns and behaviours of student disengagement, or the possible negative attitudes of parents towards education that students adopt and carry with them through schooling. The level of impact on students' educational performance is all to do with the length of time that a student is absent from school and how regularly this occurs.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: It may sound surprising, but you don't have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History. I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Richard Thompson Ford is a law professor, and you probably won't forget that for even one page. His carefully reasoned arguments, packed with examples, sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier. You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Ford's thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. Through this lens, he shows us that the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Ford takes the reader through the evolution of fashion while examining the underlying motivations of status, sex, power, and personality, which, he assumes, influenced all innovations in fashion in the past and which continue to influence us today. His writing is more than a little dense—dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. But there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. No one is spared his sharp analysis: not the easy targets of 19th century women's crippling(伤害身体的) fashions nor the modern uniforms of Silicon Valley T-shirts

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. Ford asks us to question unconscious beliefs, to realize that we almost never do so, to understand that the simplest choices are charged with meaning, and yet that meaning can and does change all the time. Consider the fact that a 1918 catalog insisted that boys and girls be dressed in the appropriate color. We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it's not.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The art of persuasion means convincing others to agree with your point of view or to follow your course of action. For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Employers place a great value on employees with persuasion skills because they can impact several aspects of job performance. Besides, teamwork and leadership rely heavily on the power of persuasion to get things done. Without persuasion skills, employees may not be as committed to or convinced of the importance of an organization's vision and long-term mission. Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: In order to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace, you need to understand how to handle conflicts and reach agreements. Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. Before you can get somebody on-board with your goal, you should help them understand why they should pursue it. Using visual aids to back up your ideas can help communicate your ideas better and make compelling arguments so your listeners will come to a logical choice and become fully committed to your ideas and plans.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Successful persuasion skills are based on your ability to have positive interactions and maintain meaningful relationships with people. In order to sustain those relationships, you must be able to work in their best interests as well. Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. The more they achieve and the greater progress they make, the more they trust your judgement and strength.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: We persuade and get persuaded every day—we're either convincing or being convinced. A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes.

questions.analysis:
【参考译文】
The Chinese character "Fu" means happiness and good fortune, and is one of the most commonly used auspicious symbols in traditional Chinese culture. People usually write a large character "Fu" on red paper, expressing their wish for family happiness, social stability and national prosperity. Pasting the character "Fu" during the Spring Festival is a long-standing folk custom. To celebrate the Spring Festival, every household pastes the character "Fu" on doors or walls, expressing their longing for a happy life and their expectation for a better future. Sometimes people also paste the character "Fu" upside down to indicate that happiness and good fortune have arrived.
